reviews.text: I came here expecting a Haebangchon feel, but it exceeded my expectations! The taste was more than basic, and the large store made conversation easy. Above all, the staff were always friendly, so I had a delicious and comfortable meal.

reviews.author: Shinnalchi
reviews.text:
A famous frozen pork belly restaurant with a generous Obon tray set that still has people waiting in line to eat.
Nowadays, it has become a national rule that side dishes are served on an Obon tray due to the retro sensibility of cold ginseng boasting a high cooking capacity, but this can be traced back to its beginnings.

On this day, I visited Haebangchon branch. Even though many directly managed stores have opened, Class still waits for customers. As soon as you eat it, you can tell that all the side dishes on the Obon tray are delicious. The first-grade raw pork belly is rapidly frozen, so it is moist and crispy instead of crumbly, so it is delicious to eat on its own, but the accompanying side dishes are also delicious when grilled together, and are especially great when dipped in egg and served with green onions like sukiyaki.

Wow, the spicy soft tofu here... drives people crazy... it's spicy and boiling with sliced ​​red peppers, topped with yellow egg yolk... it's savory and just delicious. Plus, it costs 9,000 won, serves 3 to 4 people, and tastes like a slap in the face to soft tofu restaurants, so I drink soju.

Also, you can't go to Jamsugyojip without eating fried kimchi, so you must eat it as dessert.

reviews.author: James youngho Oh
reviews.text:
- Sunday visit
- Because we visited just before lunch time, we were seated right away without waiting.
- Quick-frozen pork belly and soft tofu stew are both very good.
- I like the variety of side dishes and seasonings.
- A window seat is better.

reviews.author: Ga young Bae
reviews.text: Since the year before last, cold ginseng has become very popular, and thanks to that popularity, Jamsugyojip has opened several branches, making it a total of six. The Haebangchon branch has a good location, so I've never tried it because I always seem to wait for about an hour, but I heard that the number of people has decreased a lot due to the coronavirus these days, so I went there. I went in after checking the visitors using the QR code due to the coronavirus. I was already grilling it because my acquaintances had ordered it. First of all, there were a lot of side dishes and plenty of berries and wraps for dipping. I ordered 3 servings of pork belly, and it was so cute that the butcher came with a sticker worth looking at. At around 13,000 won per serving, it is on the expensive side for cold ginseng. It's cheap cold ginseng, but it's become much more luxurious. It was a method of putting rapidly frozen cold ginseng on a grill, seasoning it with pepper, and grilling it. The taste was so-so, but the Cheonggukjang (cheonggukjang) was really delicious. I think I used half and half soybean paste stew and cheonggukjang, and it was very delicious, with a savory, spicy flavor and soft tofu. I ordered one serving of fried rice and a fried egg and ate it all. If you don’t know anything else, be sure to order the Cheonggukjang here!! Cold ginseng was just so-so. It seems to be a place that fits well with the retro craze. The three of us drank about four or five bottles during the day, and I think it came out to about 75,000 won. After calculating the price, I was even more surprised by the price of cold ginseng...

reviews.author: Wolf Kang
reviews.text:
Frozen pork belly from Jeju, cut into squares and served in a stainless steel bowl. Heat it on a square cast iron grill covered with foil and sprinkle with McCormick pepper. When the pork belly oil starts to come out, add water parsley, dried chili peppers, green onion kimchi, etc.

I took a bite with the side dishes. And ssam made with raw garlic, seasoned green onion, and pollack roe ssamjang. A glass of soju, a full pot of cheonggukjang (cheonggukjang), and a spoonful of spicy soft tofu. There are so many delicious combinations of pork belly and soju that you won't be able to rest your hands. Then, finely chop the remaining pork belly and add savory stir-fried rice with pork fat and a fried egg.

It's an exciting place just for the food, but thanks to the old-fashioned round obon and old props hidden throughout, it's become an attractive space where soju is delicious. A house I want to go to often, but it's hard to get there because of the wait. They said they open early on Saturdays, so it's been a while since I made a reservation. The food was still good, and drinking soju while listening to Tapgol songs was also good. A Wanso restaurant that I wish existed in my neighborhood.
